mainTopic: The leniencies for טבריא, pouring water from balconies and into small courtyards on שבת, and the rule that theft gives no rights in שבת domains
overview: This amud finishes the leniencies רבי חנניה בן עקביא gave the people of טבריא. A ברייתא explains drying with a towel on שבת: the worry is wringing it out, and רבי שמעון even lets a person carry the towel home. Next, רבה בר רב הונא discusses pouring water through the balcony hole, and the גמרא brings two versions of his ruling. In both versions, רב שיזבי compares the case to an עוקה (a waste-water pit). רב then rules that two balconies far apart do not restrict each other, because a person does not restrict another 'by way of the air.' רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא teach that the law of theft applies to שבת domains, so a ruin stays with its owner. This leads to a discussion of partners who built a partition together. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a courtyard smaller than four by four אמות needs a two-סאה pit before one may pour water into it on שבת. רבה begins explaining the reason, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The people of טבריא are treated like workers saving time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion: the residents of טבריא are viewed like someone who acts only so as not to lose time from his work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of טבריא are considered like someone who does this so that he will not lose time from his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an argument that began on the previous amud. It says that whatever the people of טבריא did was done only to save work time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא discussed someone who gets up early to bring home straw or stalks that are still wet with dew, in order to store produce in them. The question is whether he wanted that dew moisture, which would make the produce susceptible to טומאה (the law of כי יותן). Most people in טבריא were ordinary laborers, so we assume they went out early only to save work time and did not want the dew. That assumption is why רבי חנניה בן עקביא could be lenient with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, the city on the כנרת whose residents received these leniencies
so that he will not lose time from his work
is considered like / is compared to

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the last piece of a discussion that started on the previous amud, so do not read it as a ruling standing on its own.

phrases.english: The people of Tiberias
are considered like one who acts so as not to lose time from his work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא כְּמִי שֶׁלֹּא יִבְטַל מִמְּלַאכְתּוֹ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of the second leniency given to טבריא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-characterizing the population: their actions are presumed to be for saving work time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The residents of טבריא are treated as acting to avoid losing work time, which justifies the leniency.

steps.title: What is the towel-drying leniency?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the third leniency in the משנה, drying oneself with a towel, and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they may dry themselves with a towel": what is this about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the third leniency from the משנה and asks for an explanation. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said "they may dry themselves with a towel" without giving details. The question is what the concern is and what exactly is permitted. The answer will show that the worry is סחיטה, wringing water out of a wet towel on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: they dry themselves (with a cloth)
a towel, especially a bath towel
what is it? (a request for an explanation)

phrases.english: "And they may dry themselves with a towel":
what is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second leniency to the third leniency listed in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the leniency of drying with a towel means and what its limits are.

steps.title: A ברייתא: dry with a towel, but don't hand it to the attendants
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person may dry himself with a towel and leave it on a window. He may not give it to bathhouse attendants, because they are suspected of wringing it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A person may dry himself with a towel and put it down on a window. He should not hand it to the bathhouse attendants, because they are suspected about that very thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. Drying with a towel is allowed, but there are precautions so that no one wrings it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drying off itself is fine. The danger is סחיטה, squeezing out the absorbed water, which is forbidden on שבת. That is why he should set the towel down on a window. The bathhouse attendants are known to wring towels out before passing them to the next customer, so he may not hand it to them.

keyTerms.meaning: window (where he leaves the towel)
bathhouse attendants
suspected (of doing something forbidden)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how חז"ל protect a permitted act (drying off) from leading to a forbidden one (סחיטה).

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: A person may dry himself with a towel,
and place it on a window.
But he may not hand it over to the bathhouse attendants,
because they are suspected regarding that matter (wringing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drying with a towel is permitted. The towel is set on a window and not handed to attendants who might wring it out.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: he may even carry the towel home
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון is more lenient: the person may even carry the towel in his hand to his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He may even bring it in his hand into his house.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion and allows more. He lets the person take the towel home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא seems to worry that if he carries the towel home, he might forget and wring it out, so it should stay at the window. רבי שמעון is not worried about that and permits taking it home. This assumes there is an עירוב or some other permitted way to carry. The word "אַף" ("even") tells us he goes one step further than the first opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: even (signals a further leniency)
brings it in his hand

steps.whatToRemember: Towel on שבת: drying is permitted, and the concern is wringing. The תנא קמא: leave the towel at the window, not with the attendants. רבי שמעון: he may even carry it home.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
He may even bring it in his hand into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף מְבִיאָהּ בְּיָדוֹ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting, more lenient opinion inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, one may carry the towel home without fear that he will wring it.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: the balcony leniency is only for drawing water
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the balcony case in the משנה, רבה בר רב הונא rules that the leniency applies only to drawing water up through the hole. Pouring water down is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: They taught this only for drawing water, but pouring water out is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a balcony over water with a partition around its hole. רבה בר רב הונא limits that leniency to drawing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows drawing water through the hole in a balcony if there is a partition around the hole. רבה בר רב הונא says this works only for drawing water up. Pouring waste water down is forbidden, because the water flows out into the sea below, a forbidden area. The partition does not solve that.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only for… (a limiting formula)
to draw / fill (water)
to pour out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the towel anymore. The גמרא has jumped back to the first leniency in the משנה, the balcony over the water.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
They taught this only for drawing water,
but to pour out (water) is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְמַלּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the towel discussion and returns to the balcony leniency in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The balcony partition permits drawing water only. Pouring water down through the hole is forbidden.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: how is this different from a waste-water pit?
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי challenges רבה בר רב הונא: why should pouring here be forbidden when pouring into an עוקה (a pit in a courtyard) is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי objected: What is the difference between this and an עוקה (a pit for waste water)?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי attacks רבה בר רב הונא's ruling by comparing it to a similar case where pouring is permitted. This sets up the next move, and the next step (step 7) answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next משנה rules that if someone digs a pit holding two סאה in a small courtyard, he may pour waste water into it on שבת. This is allowed even though the water may end up flowing out to the public area. If pouring is permitted there, רב שיזבי asks, why forbid pouring through the balcony hole, where the water likewise flows out on its own?

keyTerms.meaning: raised an objection against it
what is the difference between this and…
a pit dug to collect waste water

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi objected to it:
And what is the difference between this and a pit?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁיזְבִי: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לְעוּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the ruling of רבה בר רב הונא in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that pouring through the balcony hole is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison case: pouring into an עוקה is permitted even though the water ends up flowing out. So pouring through the balcony should be permitted too, unless a real difference can be shown.

steps.title: Water in a courtyard soaks in, water from a balcony does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב שיזבי: water poured into a courtyard pit may soak into the ground, but water poured from the balcony into the water below will certainly flow away.
steps.simpleTranslation: These (the courtyard waters) get absorbed, and these (the balcony waters) do not get absorbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. It explains why pouring into an עוקה is allowed but pouring from the balcony is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water poured into an עוקה in a courtyard may soak into the ground, so we cannot be sure it will leave the courtyard. Water poured through the balcony hole lands in the water below and will certainly flow out of the permitted area. Because the result is certain, the חכמים forbade pouring from the balcony.

keyTerms.meaning: get absorbed / soak in and disappear
these
a pit dug in a courtyard to collect water

phrases.english: These are absorbed,
phrases.notes: The water poured into the courtyard pit soaks into the ground.

phrases.english: but these are not absorbed.
phrases.notes: The water poured through the balcony hole flows away into the water below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שיזבי's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring from the balcony seemed the same as pouring into an עוקה, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the courtyard the water may soak in, so it might never leave. From the balcony it certainly flows away, so it is forbidden.

steps.title: A second version: pouring is also permitted
steps.stepSummary: Some report that רבה בר רב הונא actually said the opposite: pouring through the balcony hole is permitted too, not only drawing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבה בר רב הונא said: Do not say that only drawing water is permitted and pouring is forbidden. Rather, pouring is also permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבה בר רב הונא said. In this version, he permits both drawing water and pouring it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 5), רבה בר רב הונא permitted only drawing water and forbade pouring. In this version, he says one should not make that distinction: pouring is allowed as well. The גמרא keeps both reports side by side as two competing versions (איכא דאמרי); it does not cancel the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: to draw / fill water
to pour out
permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new teacher arguing with רבה בר רב הונא. It is a different report of what he himself said. In this version, pouring is permitted.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Do not say that it is only drawing water that is permitted,
while pouring is forbidden;
rather, pouring is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the ruling in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through the balcony hole, both drawing water and pouring water are permitted.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: this is obvious, it is just like the pit
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי objects that the second version teaches nothing new, since it is the same as the rule of the עוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said: That is obvious! It is the same as the pit!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי attacks the second version. He says it is obvious and did not need to be said, because the עוקה law already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב שיזבי used the עוקה to ask why pouring is forbidden. Now that pouring is permitted, he uses the same עוקה to ask why the rule needed to be stated at all. The complaint is פשיטא: the statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (so why say it?)
this is the same as

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said: It is obvious!
This is the same as the pit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's second version, which permits pouring
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pouring into an עוקה is already permitted, permitting pouring from the balcony adds nothing new.

steps.title: It needed to be said, because one might have split the cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without this teaching, we might have used the absorption difference to forbid the balcony. רבה בר רב הונא teaches that the cases are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: these (courtyard waters) get absorbed and these (balcony waters) do not. So he teaches us that pouring is still permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב שיזבי by explaining why the statement was needed. It uses the same distinction from step 7, but now only as a mistaken thought that the ruling corrects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the balcony is stricter, since its water does not soak in. רבה בר רב הונא teaches us not to make that distinction, so pouring is allowed in both places. The same words from step 7 now play the opposite role: there they were the real reason, and here they are the mistake being rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
it teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the absorption difference is the reason pouring from the balcony is forbidden. In the second version, it is only a mistaken thought, and pouring is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the same reasoning can be the actual ruling in one version and the rejected הוה אמינא in another.

phrases.english: You might have said:
these are absorbed and these are not absorbed,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שיזבי's challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why the statement is needed (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the teaching, we might have said the balcony is forbidden, because its water does not soak in.
steps.terutzMaskana: The absorption difference does not matter here. Pouring is permitted in both cases.

steps.title: Two balconies: the upper one is permitted if they are far apart
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה about two balconies, רב הונא in the name of רב limits the restriction to balconies that are close together. If they are separated, the upper balcony may draw water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And likewise, two balconies, one above the other, etc.' רב הונא said in the name of רב: This was taught only when the balconies are near each other. But if they are separated, the upper balcony is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, two balconies one above the other. רב explains that the restriction applies only when they are close together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that residents of both balconies may not draw water until they make a shared עירוב. רב limits this to balconies that are close together, within four טפחים sideways. If they are farther apart, the lower balcony does not restrict the upper one, so the upper residents may draw water.

keyTerms.meaning: balconies
they taught this only in the case of
near / close (within four טפחים)
separated / far apart
the upper one

phrases.english: The משנה said: And likewise, two balconies, one above the other, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, setting up רב's comment.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only when the balcony is near,
but if it is separated, the upper one is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's case of two balconies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lower balcony restricts the upper one only when they are close together. If they are separated, the upper balcony is permitted.

steps.title: רב is consistent: no restriction through the air
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב's ruling fits his general rule that one person does not restrict another by way of the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב follows his own reasoning, for רב said: A person does not restrict his fellow by way of the air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב's ruling about the two balconies fits another rule he taught elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the balconies are far apart, the lower residents could reach the upper balcony only across open air. רב holds that using a place only through the air does not let someone restrict it. That is why the upper balcony stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: following his own reasoning (he is being consistent)
restricts / forbids
by way of the air (across open space)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, being able to reach a place only across open air is not enough to restrict others from using it. So a far-away lower balcony does not restrict the upper one.

phrases.english: And Rav follows his own reasoning,
for Rav said:
A person does not restrict his fellow
by way of the air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling in step 11 by connecting it to his general rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a separated upper balcony is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's general rule: אין אדם אוסר על חבירו דרך אויר

steps.title: Theft applies on שבת, and a ruin goes back to its owner
steps.stepSummary: רבה quoting רבי חייא, and רב יוסף quoting רבי אושעיא, rule that there is 'גזל' on שבת and that a ruin is returned to its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי חייא, and רב יוסף said in the name of רבי אושעיא: There is stealing on שבת, and a ruin is returned to its owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling, reported through two chains of teachers, about using a ruin that belongs to someone else. The meaning of this short statement is unclear, and the next steps work it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a person whose house is next to someone else's abandoned ruin and who uses that ruin during the week. The ruling has two parts, 'there is theft on שבת' and 'a ruin is returned to its owner.' The גמרא will now ask how these two parts fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft; taking or using something that belongs to someone else
A ruin; a broken-down, abandoned building
Returns it to the owners
On שבת (here, about the laws of שבת domains and carrying)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about stealing an object on שבת. It is about whether using someone else's property without permission gives you rights to that space for the laws of carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbah said that Rabbi Chiyya said,
and Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
There is theft regarding Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Its exact meaning is clarified in the next two steps.

phrases.english: And a ruin is returned to its owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא, וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whether using another person's property without permission counts for שבת domains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is 'גזל' on שבת, and a ruin is returned to its owner.

steps.title: The two halves of the ruling seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that 'יש גזל בשבת' implies the user acquires the ruin, while 'returned to the owner' implies he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement contradicts itself! You said 'there is theft on שבת,' which shows that the person acquires the place. Then you said 'a ruin is returned to its owners,' which shows that he does not acquire it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling by showing that its first half and its second half seem to say opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the גמרא reads 'there is theft on שבת' as meaning that theft works on שבת: someone who took over the ruin during the week may treat it as his own on שבת. But 'returned to its owner' suggests the ruin still belongs to the owner, so the user gains nothing. Both readings cannot be true at once.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
This shows that; we can conclude
He acquires it
He does not acquire it

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said 'there is theft on Shabbat' —
this shows that he acquires it,
phrases.notes: The person who used the ruin during the week gains rights to it for שבת.

phrases.english: and 'a ruin is returned to its owners' —
this shows that he does not acquire it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 13 as internally inconsistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two-part ruling of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause seems to mean the user acquires the ruin. The second clause means he does not. The statement contradicts itself.

steps.title: The second half explains the first: the user does not gain the ruin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ruling: the law of theft applies on שבת, so the ruin stays with its owner and the user gains no rights to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they mean: The law of theft applies on שבת. How so? A ruin is returned to its owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing that the second half of the ruling explains the first half instead of opposing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יש גזל בשבת' does not mean that theft works. It means the law against theft is in force for שבת domains too, so a stolen place stays the owner's. 'Returned to its owner' is the practical example. The person who used the ruin during the week may not treat it as his own on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a rereading of the statement)
The law of theft (that stolen property must go back)
How so? In what way?

steps.whatToRemember: Final meaning: the law of theft applies to שבת domains. Using someone else's ruin without permission gives you no rights to it for שבת. It counts as the owner's.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
the law of theft applies regarding Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The key added word is דִּין, meaning the law of theft.

phrases.english: how so? —
that a ruin is returned to its owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording (הכי קאמר): the second clause explains the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יש גזל בשבת' was taken to mean that taking over a place works, so the user acquires it for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the law of theft applies, so the user does not acquire it. The ruin stays the owner's.

steps.title: רבה challenges this teaching from the two balconies
steps.stepSummary: רבה raises a difficulty from the משנה of two balconies, one above the other: if using another's space counts as theft and is ignored, why do the balconies forbid each other?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And we raised an objection against our own teaching from the משנה: 'And likewise, two balconies, one above the other, and so on.' If you say that the law of theft applies on שבת, why are they forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה, who reported the ruling, now challenges it himself using the משנה about two balconies that we already saw. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says two balconies, one above the other, forbid each other in drawing water unless they make an עירוב together. If using a neighbor's space without permission counts as theft and gives no rights, one balcony's use of the other's area should mean nothing. Then why should they restrict each other?

keyTerms.meaning: And we raised an objection against our own teaching
Balconies
One above the other
Why are they forbidden?

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the new rule about theft back to the balcony משנה that this whole sugya has been discussing (steps 11-12). It tests whether 'יש גזל בשבת' can fit with that משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbah said: And we raised an objection against our teaching:
'And likewise, two balconies
one above the other, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: they forbid each other.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ יֵשׁ דִּין גָּזֵל בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: And if you say the law of theft applies on Shabbat,
why are they forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 15 using the balcony משנה from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling 'יש דין גזל בשבת' as explained in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If using someone else's area counts as theft and gives no rights, one balcony's use of the other's area should not count. The משנה, however, says the two balconies forbid each other.

steps.title: The partition was built jointly
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה of the balconies deals with a case where both balconies' residents built the upper partition together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Here we are dealing with a case where they built the partition as partners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רבה's question from step 16. He limits the משנה of the balconies to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה asked why the lower balcony restricts the upper one, if using someone else's space is just theft and doesn't count. רב ששת answers that this is not theft at all. The lower residents helped build the upper partition, so they have real rights in it. Partners with real rights do restrict each other, so both balconies are forbidden until they make an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that limits a source to a specific case)
Partition / wall
In partnership, jointly

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the earlier principle that 'יש גזל בשבת'. Using another's space without rights gives no claim. The balcony case is different only because the residents became real partners.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's usual way of saying: let's pin down exactly which case we're talking about.

phrases.english: For example, where they made the partition in partnership.
phrases.notes: The upper and lower residents built the upper balcony's partition together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's difficulty from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers to a jointly built partition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lower residents restrict the upper ones just by using their space, which would contradict 'יש גזל בשבת'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lower residents are real co-owners of the partition, so their restriction comes from partnership, not from theft.

steps.title: Then the partnership should still apply when the lower balcony has its own partition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת: if the lower residents are partners, they should still restrict the upper ones even after the lower balcony gets its own partition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then when they made a partition for the lower balcony too, the upper should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer. It points to another case in the משנה that doesn't seem to fit his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, when the lower balcony also has a partition, the upper residents are allowed to use theirs. But if the lower residents are partners in the upper partition, building a second partition shouldn't erase that partnership. So the upper residents should still be restricted.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on the previous answer)
The lower one (here, the lower balcony)

phrases.english: If so,
when they made a partition for the lower one as well, the upper should also be forbidden!
phrases.notes: The partnership in the upper partition should still exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's explanation from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the lower residents are partners in the upper partition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A partnership doesn't disappear just because a second partition was built. So the restriction should remain, yet the משנה permits the upper balcony in that case.

steps.title: Building a separate partition ends the partnership
steps.stepSummary: Building their own partition shows the lower residents' intention that they no longer want to be partners with the upper residents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they made a partition for the lower balcony, they revealed their intention: 'I do not want to be with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Building a separate partition is a clear sign that the lower residents are giving up the partnership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their actions speak for them. By investing in their own partition, the lower residents show they want to be separate. They have effectively given up their share in the upper partition, so they no longer restrict the upper residents.

keyTerms.meaning: He clearly revealed his intention
It is not pleasing to me / I don't want it
With you

steps.whatToRemember: The lower balcony restricts the upper only because the residents are partners in the upper partition. Once the lower residents build their own partition, they show they want out of the partnership, and the restriction ends.

phrases.english: Since they made a partition for the lower one,
they clearly revealed their intention
that: 'Being with you is not what I want.'
phrases.notes: They gave up their share in the upper partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and closes the balcony discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The partnership remains even after a second partition is built.
steps.terutzMaskana: Building a separate partition shows the lower residents have given up the partnership, so the upper residents are permitted.

steps.title: Pouring water into a small courtyard on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: in a courtyard smaller than four by four אמות, one may not pour waste water on שבת unless there is a pit holding two סאה below the opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: A courtyard smaller than four אמות: one may not pour water into it on שבת unless they made a pit for it that holds two סאה from the opening downward.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: pouring waste water into a very small courtyard on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small courtyard cannot soak up the water, so the water will flow out into the public domain. That makes it look as if the person is carrying water out of his domain. A pit big enough to hold two סאה keeps the water inside the courtyard, so pouring is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Courtyard
Four cubits (here, four by four in area)
A pit or hollow dug to collect water
Two סאה (a measure of volume)
Hole / opening (here, the edge or opening of the pit)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Less than four אמות' refers to the courtyard's area, four by four. It is not a length or distance someone walks.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A courtyard that is less than four cubits (by four cubits),
one may not pour (waste) water into it on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ עוּקָה
phrases.english: unless they made a pit for it
that holds two se'a
from the opening downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חָצֵר שֶׁהִיא פְּחוּתָה מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the balcony discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waste water may not be poured into a courtyard smaller than four by four אמות on שבת unless it has a pit holding two סאה below its opening.

steps.title: The pit may be inside or outside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the required pit can be dug inside the courtyard or just outside it. If it is outside, it must be covered with an arch.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not matter whether the pit is outside or inside. The only difference: if it is outside, it must be covered with an arch; if it is inside, it does not need an arch.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from Step 20 keeps going. It explains where the two-סאה pit may be placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit's job is to catch the waste water so the water does not run out into רשות הרבים. A pit inside the courtyard already does this. A pit outside the courtyard sits in the public area, so it must be covered over (arched), so that the water is not openly flowing into רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside (here: the pit is dug outside the courtyard)
Inside (the pit is dug inside the courtyard)
To arch over, to cover with a vault

phrases.english: Whether outside or inside.
phrases.notes: Refers to the location of the two-סאה pit from Step 20.

phrases.english: Except that outside, one must arch over it,
phrases.notes: A pit in the public area must be covered.

phrases.english: inside, one does not need to arch over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, defining where the required pit may be placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pit may be inside or outside the courtyard; an outside pit must be arched over.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: one may pour into a covered drain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that if a drain is covered for its first four אמות in רשות הרבים, one may pour water into it on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: if a drain is arched over for four אמות in the public domain, one may pour water into it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the opinion of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about pouring water straight into a drain (ביב) that runs out to רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water travels through the drain under the street, and it only comes out into the open after four covered אמות. Because the water does not come out right away, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats it as acceptable to pour directly into the drain.

keyTerms.meaning: A drain or gutter channel that carries water out
Arched over, covered
The public domain

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A drain that is arched over
for four cubits in the public domain —
one may pour water into it on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related case: pouring straight into a covered drain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A drain covered for four אמות in רשות הרבים may receive poured water on שבת.

steps.title: The חכמים: never pour directly into the drain's mouth
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Even from a huge roof or courtyard, one may not pour straight into the drain's opening. One may pour onto the roof and let the water flow into the drain by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: even if a roof or courtyard is a hundred אמות, one may not pour onto the mouth of the drain. But he may pour onto the roof, and the water flows down into the drain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view of the חכמים, which completes the argument with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, pouring straight into the drain sends the water out to the public area directly by the person's own action, and the covering does not help. If he pours onto the roof and the water later runs into the drain by itself, that is permitted. Even a very large space (a hundred אמות) does not allow pouring directly into the drain.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority opinion)
The mouth or opening of the drain
Roof

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the four-אמות courtyard rule. A big courtyard lets you pour onto its ground, but even a hundred-אמה courtyard does not let you pour straight into the drain's opening.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ גַּג אוֹ חָצֵר מֵאָה אַמָּה —
phrases.english: Even a roof or a courtyard of a hundred cubits —
one may not pour onto the mouth of the drain,
but he may pour onto the roof,
and the water flows down into the drain.
phrases.notes: The water reaches the drain by itself, not by direct pouring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may never pour directly into the drain's mouth, even from a large area; pouring onto the roof so the water flows down by itself is permitted.

steps.title: A courtyard and a portico add up to four אמות
steps.stepSummary: A courtyard and the portico next to it are counted together to reach the four-אמות size that removes the need for a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A courtyard and a portico combine to make up four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה returns to the main rule about courtyard size. It tells us we may add the portico's area to the courtyard's area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard alone is less than four by four אמות but the courtyard together with the אכסדרה reaches that size, they count as one space. Then no pit is needed and one may pour water there.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico: a roofed area without walls in front of a house
They combine, they are counted together

phrases.english: The courtyard and the portico
combine for the four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the drain argument to the courtyard-size rule of Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Courtyard and portico together count toward the four-by-four-אמות minimum.

steps.title: Two upper stories: only those who built a pit may pour
steps.stepSummary: When two upper apartments face each other over one small courtyard, the residents who built a pit may pour, and the residents who did not build one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, two upper stories facing each other: some made a pit and some did not. Those who made a pit are permitted; those who did not make a pit are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case of two upper apartments sharing a small courtyard, where only one side built a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group is judged by its own pit. The ones who built a pit have a place for their water, so they may pour. The others have no pit, so they may not pour. Building a pit is what allows pouring in a small courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper stories, upper apartments
One opposite the other, facing each other
A pit dug to collect water

steps.whatToRemember: Summary of the משנה: a courtyard under four by four אמות needs a two-סאה pit before one may pour water on שבת. The pit may be inside, or outside if it is arched over. The חכמים forbid pouring straight into a drain. A courtyard and portico combine to reach four אמות. Each resident's permission depends on his own pit.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי דְיוֹטָאוֹת זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ,
phrases.english: And likewise, two upper stories opposite one another,
some of them made a pit
and some of them did not make a pit,
those who made a pit are permitted,
those who did not make a pit are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי דְיוֹטָאוֹת זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the משנה, applying the pit rule to two groups of residents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Residents who built a pit may pour; those who did not are forbidden.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the four-אמות rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why a courtyard of four by four אמות does not need a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule without a reason: four אמות, no pit needed; less than four, a pit of two סאה is needed. The גמרא wants to know why exactly these measurements matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that follows the משנה
What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why four by four אמות frees a courtyard from needing a pit, and why the pit must hold two סאה.

steps.title: רבה: people use two סאה a day and like to sprinkle it
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that a person usually uses about two סאה of water a day. In a courtyard of four אמות, he is glad to sprinkle that water on the ground. (The answer continues on the next amud.)
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Because a person usually uses two סאה of water each day. In a space of four אמות, a person wants to sprinkle the water,
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins answering the question. He explains where the two-סאה measure comes from and why four אמות matters. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two סאה is the normal daily amount of water a person uses, so a pit of that size can hold it all. In a courtyard of four by four אמות, the person actually wants to spread the water on the ground to settle the dust. So even if some water runs out to the street, that is not what he intends, and no pit is required.

keyTerms.meaning: To use, to make use of
Two סאה (a measure of volume)
To sprinkle them (the water) on the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: רבה's reason explains both numbers in the משנה: the pit size (two סאה = a day's water) and the courtyard size (four אמות = enough space where a person wants to sprinkle the water).

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Because a person usually makes use of
two se'a of water every day,
phrases.notes: This is why the pit must hold two סאה.

phrases.english: in four cubits, a person wants to sprinkle it,
phrases.notes: Sprinkling settles the dust; the statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָדָם עָשׂוּי לְהִסְתַּפֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person uses two סאה of water daily; in a four-אמות courtyard he wants to sprinkle it on the ground, so the outflow is not his intention (continues on the next amud).
